parole.testo: From Old Norse fangelsi, fanga (“capture, seize”) + -elsi (suffix from Proto-West Germanic *-islī), really the Old West Norse form of Old Swedish fangilse (13th c.). Cognate to Swedish fängelse.
From Old Norse frjádagr, from Proto-West Germanic *Frījā dag (“day of Frigg”).
From Old Norse keppa, from Proto-West Germanic *kampijan.

parole.significato: to make ferment, to bury and allow to ferment
parole.testo: From an unattested Old Norse *kæsa (compare Faroese kæsa (“to press cheese”)), a back-formation from kæsir (“rennet”) (< Proto-West Germanic *kāsī < Latin cāseus), which has been reinterpreted as an agent noun and assumed to have been derived from a verb.

From Old Norse lortr, cognate with Faroese lortur (“excrement, feces”), Danish lort (“excrement, feces”). From Old Norse mánadagr, from Proto-West Germanic *mānini dag, a calque of Latin dies lunae. Compare Faroese mánadagur, Danish and Norwegian Bokmål mandag, Swedish and Norwegian Nynorsk måndag.
From sunna (“sun”) + dagur (“day”). From Old Norse sunnudagr, from Proto-West Germanic *sunnōn dag, a calque of Latin dies Solis.
From Old Norse týsdagr, from Týr (“Tyr”) and dagr (“day”), from Proto-West Germanic *Tīwas dag, a calque of Latin dies Martis.

From Old Norse þórsdagr (“Thor's day, day of Thor”) Þórr (“Thor”) (modern Icelandic Þór) and dagr (“a day”) (modern Icelandic dagur (“a day”)). Corresponds to Proto-West Germanic *Þunras dag (“day of the thunder god”), calque of Latin dies Iovis.
